🚇 AI Idea Flow · 1950 → 2026

How AI's Ideas Flowed and Merged, from 1950 to Today

Scroll down from today back to the first ideas of 1950, seventy-six years of AI research drawn as a metro map. Each coloured line is a research area, each bubble is a landmark paper, and the bigger the bubble, the more later ideas were built directly on it. Streams of light run down every line, and glowing links carry ideas from where they began to what they made possible. Where a link crosses to another line, two fields merged into something new. Click any bubble to open its family tree.

🌌 See it in 3D
Lines:
Jump to:
Bubble size = how many ideas built directly on it Ringed = merges two or more fields Flow: origin (below) → later idea (above) ★ prize-recognised

Tap a bubble to open its family tree. Pick up to three lines above to keep the map readable.

How to read this map: bubbles are the paper cards from the AI Research Progress Through the Years articles, so the map shows what that series covers, not all of AI. Bubble size counts how many other cards in the series were built directly on that idea. That measures influence within this series, not real-world citations, and recent ideas have had little time to be built on. The links are our editorial reading of each paper's lineage — direct building blocks, methods it combined, or ideas it replaced — and influence is often shared and debatable. The lines are broad research areas we assigned, and many papers could sit on two. Years with no cards are skipped, so spacing is by row, not by calendar. "Key ideas" is a curated subset; the family tree always shows every link.
